A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spline-encoding study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on 25 tabular datasets, synthetic encoding comparisons and ablations, and SGEMM training-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark, synthetic, ablation, and timing results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed spline families, knot-placement procedures, softmax-cumulative-sum parameterization, training objective, and spacing regularizer remain unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 clarify notation and exposition without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 regression and 12 classification datasets, SGEMM efficiency setting, and synthetic tasks. V2's new Figure 1 illustrates encoding coordinates without a target, predictive model, or evaluation split; it adds no evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The same 14 main-benchmark methods and the same ablation and efficiency comparators are reported. Newly discussed architectures such as TabM are not evaluated. The revised PLE boundary specification is a preprocessing-definition change, not an added comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D revises the stated PLE preprocessing rule: v1 permits extrapolation through the first and last bin coordinates, whereas v2 saturates them at 0 and 1. Splits, metrics, architectures, and training budgets are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that this documentation revision involved rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: The synthetic PLE/B-spline comparison, resolution sweep, SGEMM efficiency analysis, and knot-learning-rate illustration are retained. The new encoding schematic and average-rank tables do not introduce an additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain five-fold mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, five-seed resolution experiments, single-seed knot trajectories, and Friedman/Nemenyi testing. The added rank tables do not change statistical estimation or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in v1 Tables 7–13 match v2 Tables 11–17, and all original result figures are retained unchanged. V2 Tables 9–10 redisplay the existing critical-difference diagram ranks with finer rounding, rather than adding different findings.

T1.justification: Appendix D corrects the false claim that cumulative PLE has at most two nonzero components to the property that at most one component is fractional, and revises its boundary definition. Section 3.1.4 also adds the necessary condition 0 < delta < 1/(K_j + 1) for the spacing construction.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and task/backbone-dependence claims remain. The revised conclusion adds a more prescriptive contribution: B-splines provide an efficient regression starting point, with I-splines and learnable knots reserved for selected higher-budget settings.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 and new Table 2 expand practical selection guidance, including recommendations for architectures not evaluated here. Section 7 newly explains that feature-wise encodings leave interactions to the backbone and discusses joint encodings and their dimensionality costs.

D1.justification: The implementation pointer changes from an anonymized repository to a named GitHub repository. New Appendix E documents the synthetic sample and encoding settings used for Figure 1. Existing hardware, optimization, architecture, and benchmark configuration details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations connecting numerical encodings to positional encodings, RoPE, and Fourier features, plus references concerning TabM and feature interactions. The central positioning of explicit spline preprocessing relative to architectural spline components is retained.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reworks the methodological exposition around feature-wise encoding and consistent sample, feature, and basis notation, extending this treatment through the appendices and algorithms. It also condenses the abstract, reorders related-work discussion, and rewrites the conclusion and limitations.

P2.justification: V2 adds an encoding schematic, a practical-recommendations table, a notation table, and two tables redisplaying existing ranks. Original result graphics and detailed result-table structures remain intact, with adjusted placement, numbering, and corrected cross-references.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency through the PLE-property correction and explicit spacing constraint. Its schematic, notation table, and interaction limitation also improve clarity. The empirical evidence is unchanged, while recommendations for unevaluated TabM, TabTransformer, and SAINT extend beyond the demonstrated coverage, limiting the overall gain.
